newsitem.title: CHINA: Australia PM tours Shanghai, says China ties grow.
newsitem.headline: Australia PM tours Shanghai, says China ties grow.

text.p: Australia's Prime Minister John Howard toured China's financial centre of Shanghai on Saturday, and said economic and air links between the two countries were growing fast.

"The dramatic growth in air travel between Australia and China is just another element in a deepening economic and trade association," he said at a ceremony to mark the opening of an Ansett Australia airline office in Shanghai.
When Ansett air services between Sydney and Shanghai begin in June, there will be four airlines operating a total of seven services a week between the two countries, he said.

Howard, who is on a four-day visit to China, also visited a building materials factory run by the Australian firm BHP in Shanghai's Pudong development zone, which has grown from paddy fields to a major industrial base over the past five years.

"This is probably the most rapidly industrialising part of the world," he told reporters. "If Australia is to be relevant in this part of the world, then obviously it has to be part of the economic action."
